memories.memory_text: I dove out the Stonebridge House window with Spencer Foster just as it exploded, grabbing a cable to start sliding down the building.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway collide with a large banner, causing it to detach and carry them toward the street.
memories.memory_text: I collided with Spencer Foster into a huge 'GRAND OPENING' banner, we slammed against it, and I felt it break loose as we started falling together toward the street.

grounded_facts: The cable supporting Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway breaks, causing them to swing uncontrollably toward a banner.
memories.memory_text: I screamed when the cable broke and we started swinging uncontrollably toward the banner, then I saw a huge truck speeding at us as Spencer Foster and I hung on for our lives.

grounded_facts: As Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway fall toward the street, a speeding truck passes beneath them, narrowly missing them.
memories.memory_text: I was falling with Spencer Foster toward the street when I saw a huge truck speeding toward us, and I barely lifted my feet in time as it passed beneath us.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway fall directly into the open sunroof of a large stretch limo, surviving the fall.
memories.memory_text: I was falling with Spencer Foster after we got knocked off the sign, and I remember holding on for my life as a truck sped toward us—we barely lifted our feet in time, and then the sign dipped and we dropped straight through the open sunroof of a stretch limo.

grounded_facts: A moment of relief and reorientation for Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway immediately following a life-threatening event, marked by their survival and transition to a new location.
memories.memory_text: I remember slamming into the seat and struggling to catch my breath, then starting to laugh with Spencer Foster when I realized we were still alive.

grounded_facts: Reese Calloway confirms to Spencer Foster that they survived the recent danger.
memories.memory_text: I told Spencer Foster, 'We made it, man,' just to confirm we both knew we'd survived.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway discover that the Micah Cavendish and four friends are already in the limo with them, changing their perception of the situation.
memories.memory_text: I was with Spencer Foster when we got into the limo, and I looked up to see the Micah Cavendish and four of his friends already sitting there, staring at us, which completely changed how I saw the situation.

grounded_facts: The Micah Cavendish expresses relief that Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway survived, implying a sense of fate or divine intervention.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Micah Cavendish say, 'Well, there is a God after all,' as if our survival was meant to be.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway arrive at the Red Dragon hotel in a limousine, witnessing emergency vehicles and arrests outside.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Micah Cavendish and his friends already in the limo, then exchanged a look with Spencer Foster as we stopped in front of the Red Dragon hotel, where I heard someone say, 'Here we are. The Red Dragon hotel.'

grounded_facts: The Micah Cavendish invites Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway to join his group for gambling and a Siegfried and Roy show.
memories.memory_text: I was invited by the Micah Cavendish to join his group for gambling and then to see Siegfried and Roy—he said he hoped Spencer Foster and I were feeling lucky.

grounded_facts: Reese Calloway playfully accuses Spencer Foster of being kissed by Shawn Hayes, lightening the mood during their farewell.
memories.memory_text: I saw that kiss and teased Spencer Foster about it, saying he played it cool walking away without looking back.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster gives his father's badge to Reese Calloway, symbolizing his emotional release from the past.
Spencer Foster gives Reese Calloway his father's badge as a token of trust and brotherhood.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Foster handing me his father's badge and telling me he could finally let it go — it meant a lot, like he was trusting me with something real, a symbol of our brotherhood.

grounded_facts: Reese Calloway gives Spencer Foster approximately fifty thousand dollars in cash won from gambling, encouraging him to enjoy life.
Reese Calloway gives Spencer Foster a wad of cash won from gambling to encourage him to enjoy life.
memories.memory_text: I gave Spencer Foster about fifty thousand dollars I won at the tables, telling him to enjoy life — and when he tried to refuse, I showed him I had more, saying they owe us anyway.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster reveals his long-held desire to visit Madison Square Garden to see the Knicks play, indicating a shift toward personal fulfillment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Foster telling me he always wanted to go to Madison Square Garden to see the Knicks play.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway exchange ideas about food and luxury in New York, bonding over a shared fantasy of vacation.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Spencer Foster mentioned wanting some Mu-shu, I joked about Kung-Pao, and we both smiled—our own little fantasy about New York coming alive.

grounded_facts: Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway part ways at the Las Vegas airport after completing their mission, sharing emotional goodbyes and symbolic gestures.
memories.memory_text: I said goodbye to Spencer Foster at the Las Vegas airport after watching Shawn Hayes board her plane; I bowed to him, he shook my hand like a brother and gave me his father's badge, and I gave him about fifty grand from my Fairview School winnings, telling him it was okay because I had lots more.

memories.memory_text: I tried hitting on those girls in Chinese—said something about drinks, I think—and they freaked out and sped off. I was just using the dictionary, man, how was I supposed to know it came out wrong?
I chucked Spencer Foster’s Beach Boys CD out the sunroof because he keeps playing that crap—told him I warned him about it. He got mad, like it was some sacred relic or something.

I sat down next to two guys who looked like they meant business, cracked a joke about blending in—how could I? I’m twice the size of everyone here—and asked them how they were doing. They didn’t say a word.
I pointed at the guy on stage butchering Michael Jackson and said it sounded like prison noise after lights out. Nobody even looked at me—those thugs just kept ignoring me like I wasn’t there.
I was killing it on that karaoke stage, moonwalking and locking eyes with a few women who were into it—Spencer Foster had to physically pull me off while I was in the middle of a move.

I snatched Spencer Foster's badge and the weathered radio before he could stop me, jumped back on stage, fired shots into the ceiling, and started yelling at the crowd in broken Chinese—then had to whisper and ask what the hell I'd actually said.

I was just getting to the edge to check on Spencer Foster when something hard slammed into my head—next thing I know, I'm flying off the roof, wind rushing past me before I barely caught that damn bamboo pole.

I'm hanging there, gripping that bending bamboo pole, Spencer Foster right beside me—both of us dangling over a filthy dumpster, and all I can think is, 'I came ten-thousand miles for mu-shu and this is what I get?'

I remember sitting in Spencer Foster's car, still sore and covered in garbage, when he dropped the news about the embassy bombing—two translators dead—and all I could think was, 'Of course this is tied to Carson Thorne, because why wouldn't it be?'
I had two Nico Thorne under each arm in choke holds, more pinned beneath me — one under my legs, others under my hands, the last one under my ass. They weren't going anywhere.
I told them to start practicing the LAPD choke hold and not to make me come back — then Spencer Foster shows up asking if I'm ready to have fun. Like I wasn't already running the show.
I told that smug little prick Carson Thorne to get on his feet, and when he ignored me, I grabbed his laptop and smashed it against the wall—glass and plastic went everywhere.
I called Spencer Foster out for being a lonely workaholic, asking when he last had a date or any fun—man looked like he’d never heard of a weekend.
After I told him he ain't black, we just stood there—silent, tense—like something broke between us, and then he stormed out, slamming the door.

I was standing in Diel's office, cracking jokes about dinner and biscuits and gravy while he grilled me about being in Hong Kong, and I could tell he was one step away from blowing his top over those first-class upgrades.

I saw Carson Thorne slip out of that massage parlor and jump into a Daimler—no hesitation, like he owned the damn street. I wasn’t waiting around anymore; I stepped into the road and flagged a cab, done playing by the rules.

I stepped up behind Spencer Foster when he had that Evan Calloway pinned, and I told the guy to stop playing games or we’d kick his ass—then Spencer Foster turns around, looks at me like he’s seen a ghost, and says my name like it means something.

Spencer Foster stared at me and said 'Not Yu. You!' like I was the one who got killed, and I shot back that nobody understands him anyway—then those four goons showed up with the weathered key, and I knew this was way bigger than some dead cop.
I pulled Spencer Foster aside and asked him if he was serious about meeting Carson Thorne alone after we got beat up naked—like that wasn’t some twisted welcome bonus.
When Spencer Foster said Carson Thorne was his father's old partner, I just stared at him—didn't know what to make of it, didn't say a word, just walked away.
Alex Prescott told me I was off the case and to get back to L.A., and all I said was 'Fine with me'—like I didn’t care, like I wasn’t just tossed aside after everything that went down.

Spencer Foster stepped in to take me to the airport instead of the cops, and when I flipped on him, calling his mama into it, things got real close to exploding—something in his face cracked, like he was holding back more than just anger.

I told Spencer Foster my theory—Follow the RichWhiteMan, all one word—and he actually tried saying it, stumbling over the mashup like it was some kind of code. I could tell he was skeptical, but I made it stick with the bit about white people screaming during shootings, and yeah, I ribbed him about Godzilla too.

I was holding the binoculars, scanning the city, and there it was—Kendall Ellison Towers. I knew that hotel meant Kendall Ellison was our guy. Spencer Foster wanted answers, and I pointed it out like it was obvious, right after they brought me gefilte fish and lox—I even offered him some, smearing it on a bagel like we weren’t in the middle of a chase.

I was holding that thing as far from my body as I could, looking over the edge to see if I could just chuck it — but there were people everywhere, man, I wasn't trying to drop a the blue case on some poor guy walking his dog.
She opened her robe and showed a badge pinned to her bra — I didn't trust it at first, told her to let me see it again, like, who flashes a Redwood Department badge from their underwear?
I remember Shawn Hayes lighting a hundred-dollar bill on fire and it burning red—some special ink from India, she said. That’s how you can tell the fakes; real ones burn black.
She handed Spencer Foster a card and said we were now working for the Redwood Department—me and Spencer Foster, officially recruited on the spot. I didn’t say yes, but we walked out like we were in.
I was about to shout that I'm LAPD just to see the place erupt in panic—figured it'd be hilarious—when Valerie Arden grabbed my shoulder and yanked me aside.
Valerie Arden stepped back and threw a fast martial arts move at me, so quick I didn't even have time to react — Spencer Foster had to jump in front and block it.

After Valerie Arden showed off his moves and started laughing with Spencer Foster, I remember thinking this whole thing was falling apart — I came in serious, and now they're joking about 'Reese Calloway' like we're at a damn reunion.

I felt the crack of her punch across my jaw—damn, that hit set my teeth on fire—and then she kicked me hard enough to send me flying back. I tasted blood and thought, 'This bitch is gonna pay for my dental work.'
I was walking past her, hands up, playing it cool—then *wham*—she cold-cocked me from behind. Didn't even see it coming. One second I'm moving, the next I'm on the ground, ears ringing.

I told Spencer Foster straight up—we’re not partners, not friends, not brothers. After everything, all that crap about loyalty and bonding, I had to make it clear I didn’t sign up for any of that emotional garbage.

I asked Spencer Foster if they have a 'Chinese heaven' and whether it’s like a five-foot-and-under basketball league—then we ended up talking about steamed dumplings and his sad little love life. If we were gonna die, at least I’d go mocking something.

I looked up at that neon dragon blazing over the strip and knew we couldn't just walk in looking like sewer rats — if we're gonna play rich, we gotta look the part. So I told Spencer Foster, 'Follow me, my Asian brother,' and started moving, making sure he knew I was in charge now.

I told those clipboard jockeys I was the lead singer and got held up at a wedding in Tai Koo—Parker Mercer was waiting for me, had to sell it like I was already pissed off about last time’s playlist disaster.
I grabbed that doorman by the collar, told him I wasn’t the help—I was the star, then dropped a smoking dance move right there to shut him up; he couldn’t even shake his head ‘yes’ to saving his job.
I yelled 'I wouldn't do that!!!' when Shawn Hayes started opening the the paper photograph—didn't know if it was live, but I wasn't about to watch her blow us all up just to prove a point.
After she showed that stupid stack of cash, I didn't buy it—I told her to let me see her badge again, because anyone can pin something to their bra and call themselves Redwood Department.
I pried open the crate and saw stacks of superfills—real or fake, didn’t matter—tossed a bundle to Spencer Foster and said, 'Hello, Kendall Mercer,' just to mess with him.
Spencer Foster called me a mama's boy after saying some nonsense about a Chinese man inventing electricity, and I told him not to talk about my mama—even though I winked right after.

memories.memory_text: I took a bite of my pork bao and didn’t turn around until after the explosion—when I finally looked, the vendor was already frozen in shock, so I told him to call the police.
I heard a shout—'Stop! LAPD!'—as I turned the corner with the others, but I didn’t break stride, the city dark around me and the chase already underway.
I swung the bamboo pole hard into Spencer Foster just as he pulled himself up—felt it connect, saw him topple over the edge without a sound.
Reese Calloway came bursting through the door shouting, but I was already behind him—kicked him hard in a spinning motion and sent him flying off the roof to dangle beside Spencer Foster.

I approached Kendall Ellison on the yacht, and as I got close, his smile dropped—his eyes went cold, dead. He leaned in and whispered something, then dismissed the woman beside him before she walked away.
I burst onto the deck and fired into Carson Thorne’s chest as he tried to speak—my shots cut him off mid-sentence, and he went over the rail into the water.
As Spencer Foster moved toward me, I turned away while my bodyguards rushed in from all sides to swarm him—I left as they closed in.
I was moving fast down the hallway, rounding the corner, when something caught my leg and I went flying—slammed face-first into the floor.
I snapped into a backflip, launching myself up and driving my foot into Reese Calloway's head before he could react.
I leapt onto the speedboat as it pulled away, feeling the jolt of impact under my feet while Spencer Foster shouted after me from the deck above.
I punched Reese Calloway hard across the jaw, then kicked him down—he tasted blood, and I made sure he felt every second of it.
After knocking Reese Calloway out with my the weathered radio, I gave the order—'Put them in the truck'—and watched them be carried away, powerless.

I charged Reese Calloway, sliced the roulette wheel in half, and stabbed him. He fell back. As I windmilled, a bamboo pole from a Terra Cotta soldier ricocheted and pierced my shoulder. I dropped to my knees, staring at him in disbelief.

I walked toward them, blood soaking through my clothes, the heavy weight of the paper photograph in my hand—Spencer Foster and Reese Calloway turned, and I told him, 'We'll go together, Spencer Foster.'
I pressed the switch, feeling the surge begin, and I started to smile—watching them run like cowards toward the window.
I took a bite of my pork bao just as the sixth floor of the embassy exploded behind me, and I didn’t turn quickly—just slow enough to see the vendor’s face before saying he should call the police.
I rounded the corner with the Jonah Hollis, moving fast, knowing Spencer Foster was behind us—he was chasing, but I wasn’t slowing down.
I swung the bamboo pole hard and felt it connect—Spencer Foster went over the edge fast, no time to react. He didn’t even see me coming.
Reese Calloway thought he had control, but I moved behind him silently—then one kick, spinning hard, and he was flying off the roof just like Spencer Foster. Watching them both dangle was satisfying.
I heard Kendall Ellison whisper his order, and immediately swept the room—eyes moving, hands ready—checking for threats before he even finished speaking.
I burst onto the deck and fired into Carson Thorne’s chest as he screamed at me in Chinese — he didn’t get to beg, not even for a second.
I turned and left as Spencer Foster lunged toward me — my bodyguards swarmed him from all sides, buying me time to get out.
I was moving fast down the hallway when something caught my leg and I went flying, face-first into the floor.
I flipped back up and kicked him in the head before he could react.
I remember the way Reese Calloway's body gave under my strikes—each blow driving him back, his taunts turning to grunts, the hallway echoing with the sound of flesh meeting force.
I leapt onto the speeding boat as it pulled away, the engine roar drowning out Spencer Foster’s shout—I didn’t look back.
I stepped forward and punched Reese Calloway hard across the jaw, dropping him to one knee, then kicked him backward to make sure he knew his place.
After Reese Calloway walked past me toward the truck, I swung my the weathered radio and coldcocked him—just as he thought he was safe.
I told them the plates are safe and the dragon's been fed before hanging up the phone—mission confirmed, no room for doubt.
I motioned to a monitor showing Kendall Ellison walking down the hallway toward the Stonebridge House and said in Chinese, 'He's going for the plates.'
I had the detonator in my hand, and then a sharp impact knocked it away—Shawn Hayes’s heel flashed, and it was gone, flying out the broken window.
I charged Reese Calloway, sliced his roulette wheel in half, and jabbed him with the sword. He screamed and fell back against the table.

I windmilled to kick a Terra Cotta soldier onto Reese Calloway, but the bamboo pole ricocheted—suddenly I felt a searing pain as the blade pierced through my shoulder; I dropped to my knees, stunned, then blacked out after a kick to the head.
I walked toward them, blood soaking through my clothes, the heavy weight of the larger the blue case in my hand—Spencer Foster’s eyes finally locking onto me, realizing I wasn’t finished.
I pressed the switch and felt the corner of my mouth rise—just before they turned and ran for the window.

memories.memory_text: I told Casey Colter it's my responsibility—those words came out before I even thought them, but I meant them. Carson Thorne is tied to me, and this case is mine now.
I smiled at Reese Calloway when I said we didn't take the case—told him we were going to a club instead. I could see he didn't believe me, but I had to say it.
Reese Calloway lunged and took my badge and the weathered radio before I could stop him—I didn’t even see his hands move.
I stood on that stage under the lights, translating Reese Calloway’s threats while the room stared at us, silent and dangerous.
I flung two of the Jonah Hollis off the scaffolding after wrestling them for control of the bamboo pole.
I stomped on the floorboards to unbalance the last two Jonah Hollis, then knocked them off with my pole.

I asked Sage Whitaker about Carson Thorne, needing to know how to find him, but then he said it wasn't Parker Mercer—he was the best I ever trained—no, Skyler Hollis. My father and Carson Thorne were his favorite students. I couldn't let him keep talking about the past; I just needed to know where to go.
I saw Reese Calloway with students pinned every which way, and I couldn't help but call out to him — he looked like he was having a damn field day.
I saw Carson Thorne across the room—sitting there calm, dressed in silk, laptop on his knees. I knew right away he was the one, and I told Reese Calloway we needed backup.
I left Reese Calloway behind to call for backup, but I could already tell he was going to do something reckless—I heard him confront Carson Thorne before I even reached the door.
I snapped at Reese Calloway, telling him to stop—I'm sick of his bullshit—because he doesn't get why I do things this way. It's not about fun, it's my job.
I told him he wouldn't understand my life because he's not Chinese—then he shot back 'And you ain't black!' I didn't answer. I just walked out and slammed the door.

I was walking back from the Micah Brooks's office when the explosion hit—glass and debris flying, the heat blasting my face as I hit the ground. I saw my office was gone, just smoke and fire, and I started screaming Reese Calloway's name.
I remember asking if Alex Prescott was told, and when Casey Colter said no, I knew this was our chance—I hung up and turned the music up loud, feeling the beat drive the focus I needed.

I had the Evan Calloway pinned, demanding to know where Carson Thorne was, and then I heard Reese Calloway's voice—'Yeah. Tell us!'—and when I turned, he was right there, alive. I couldn't believe it—my own voice cracked as I said, 'Reese Calloway?'

One second I was staring at Reese Calloway, trying to process that he wasn't dead, and then I heard 'Get your hands in the air'—I turned and saw four armed Harper Davenport pointing the weathered key at us. There was no time to react, only to move into position beside him.
Carson Thorne told me he didn't blow up the embassy, that there's a war within the Crown Hill Council and he's going to lose — his name's already in the book of death.
Casey Finch burst in with Jordan Carver, screamed at Carson Thorne in Chinese, then shot him in the chest — I moved toward her, but the bodyguards swarmed me before I could stop her.
I took down the first Evan Calloway, but there was no time to breathe—two more were on me, and I had to keep moving to stay alive.
Alex Prescott told me I was off the case and said he never wanted to see me again. I watched him walk away. Casey Colter ordered officers to escort Reese Calloway, and I said I'd take him.

I told Reese Calloway that Carson Thorne killed my father — I said it after he mocked me, after he got in my face, and I finally spoke the truth no one else knew, even though he didn't want to hear it.

I told Reese Calloway my fiancée left me a month before our wedding, and that I haven’t had mu-shu since — it just came out while I was holding the binoculars, like the food was easier to say than the pain.

I was watching Shawn Hayes through the binoculars, then handed them back — I saw her talking with Kendall Ellison, saw him kiss her on the cheek before he left the room, and something about it stuck with me, though I didn’t say a word.
I grabbed the paper photograph from Reese Calloway and rolled it across the roof, diving to the ground right after—didn't know if it would blow up any second.
I told Shawn Hayes I was a detective in Hong Kong—she called me 'Spencer Foster,' and I knew I wasn't letting this go, not after coming this far.

I stepped in front of Reese Calloway when Valerie Arden threw that fast martial arts move — I blocked it clean and saw he knew real technique, so I asked where he learned that Twisting Tiger. When he said Freddy Ching in Crenshaw, I couldn't help but smile and laugh with him.
Reese Calloway pressed Valerie Arden for information. Valerie Arden mentioned the funny money and said Teddy Wu was making counterfeit twenties. I stayed quiet and watched.
I told Reese Calloway I'm not used to having a partner. He said we're not partners and that all partners get you is dead. I said fine.

I asked Reese Calloway if he thought I had a good voice, and he looked at me like I was crazy. I told him to forget it, but then he said I had a pretty good voice—still, I turned away before he could see my face.
I took a breath, found the weak spot in the crate, and punched through the wood—just like striking an opponent. Focus. One perfect strike.
I told Reese Calloway he'd been a good friend, and he got defensive, but then he winked after I insulted his mama—just like us. That felt right.
I climbed out of the manhole and saw the Strip—lights everywhere, so bright I had to shield my eyes. I just said, 'Vegas...'
I turned and suddenly there it was—a massive dragon, ten stories tall, fire blasting from its nose right in front of us.
I held Shawn Hayes in my arms after dipping her, and when she asked if I’d help the Redwood Department, I told her no—but I’d help her. I meant it.

After Shawn Hayes left, Reese Calloway confronted me about dancing. I told him she said the plates were in the soft count room and pointed out the guard by the door. He offered to cause a scene at the craps table to distract security. I told him to keep them busy for five minutes.
I remember asking if Alex Prescott was told, and when Casey Colter said to let him find out on his own, I knew this was our move—I hung up and turned the music up loud, locking in.
I grabbed the paper photograph from Reese Calloway and rolled it across the roof, diving to the ground as it slid to a stop right in front of Shawn Hayes.
I told Shawn Hayes I'm a detective in Hong Kong and that I'm not walking away from this case, even after she revealed she's a Redwood Department agent.
Five years ago, Carson Thorne bought the U.S. Treasury Intaglio press—right before he left the force.
I held Shawn Hayes in my arms, her face close to mine, and when she asked if I’d help the Redwood Department, I told her no—but I’d help her. I meant it.

After Shawn Hayes left, Reese Calloway confronted me about dancing instead of working. I told him the plates are in the soft count room, and he agreed to create a distraction at the craps table so I could move.
